documents.title: Velká Británie — Skotsko, Londýn a York
documents.text: Skotsko je krajina, která se ti dostane pod kůži — Highlands, Loch Ness, hrady na skalnatých výběžcích. Počasí se mění každých dvacet minut, ale o to víc si vážíš každého průhledu mezi mraky. Londýn není potřeba představovat. Westminster, Tower, Tower Bridge, Temže — všechno v jednom dlouhém dni pěšky. Britská železnice tě tam dostane snadno, jen mind the gap . Birmingham a střední Anglie — industriální dědictví, kanály (víc než v Benátkách, prý) , méně turistů, autentičtější. „Skotsko si nemusíš pamatovat, stačí si vzpomenout, co jsi cítil."

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.text: AI in practice · explanations and guides

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.section: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.text: Find your way around the tools, write better requests and understand what AI agents can do. With simple examples you can try yourself. Prepared by Budinský Luděk · Updated 27 October 2026 Choose where you want to go 01 Communicate with AI Requests, context and checking the answer. 02 Understand the tools Models, chats, agents and their capabilities. 03 Bring AI into your work Development, repeatable workflows and automation.

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.section: First step: a small task with a clear result
documents.text: Start with a task where you can judge whether the answer makes sense, such as shortening your own text or comparing two offers you provide.

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.text: Provide the text, table or situation. Explain who the result is for and what must stay unchanged. “Shorten this email to five sentences. Keep the meeting date and a polite tone.”

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.text: Instead of “make it better”, say what you want: a short proposal, a list of questions or a comparison table. “List the differences in price, terms and anything missing from the offer.”

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.text: Check names, numbers and meaning. If something is wrong, give specific feedback and ask for that part to be corrected. “Point two is missing transport. Add it and leave the other points unchanged.” Fluent writing does not prove accuracy. AI may invent a detail or misunderstand the request. Ask it to separate supported information from assumptions. Check important facts against the original material or a reliable source.

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.text: A good request includes the goal, source material, boundaries and a way to check the result. You do not need a long list of magic phrases.

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.text: Paste two real offers into the template. AI should use their contents and point out missing terms. Before booking, check the price and availability directly with the provider. This example shows how to work with source material; it does not place a booking. Context is the background and source material AI should use. For editing text, provide the original wording and intended reader; for code, the related files and a description of the bug. Include relevant information and remove unnecessary personal details. During longer work, regularly summarise what is still valid and what has changed.

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.text: These terms are often mixed up. The distinction explains why the same AI can only answer in one setting but edit a file in another.

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.text: Generates answers from the supplied input. The model affects capability, speed and cost.

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.text: The application where you communicate with AI. Depending on the product and account, it may also offer files, search or other tools.

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.text: Works in repeated steps: proposes an approach, uses an available tool, reads the result and continues.

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.text: Determines which files, commands and services AI can access and what permissions it has. One example of a tool for working on a project is Claude Code . Always check the specific product’s capabilities in its documentation.

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.section: From a single answer to an AI agent
documents.text: An agent needs an achievable goal and clear boundaries. For example, summarise the documents it can access and save a draft in a specified folder. Understand the goal Use a tool Check the result Continue or finish “Review these documents, list the deadlines and cite the source for each one. Save the result as a draft. Do not edit the documents or send messages to anyone.” The task has a specific output. Reading material and preparing a draft require different permissions from deleting, sending or paying. Automate a repeated task only after verifying one complete run. Tasks can be split, but someone must combine the results and resolve disagreements. For a small change, one clearly defined task may be easier to follow. Splitting work makes sense when the parts are genuinely independent and their outputs can be checked.

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.section: Developing through requests: after the first draft
documents.text: In so-called vibe coding, you describe the desired behaviour in ordinary language and AI helps prepare the code. You need to be able to judge what the result actually does.

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.text: Shows the appearance and a basic flow using test data. Helps assess whether the idea is usable.

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.text: Also needs data storage and recovery, error handling, correct calculations and checks of repeated use. Describe how to reproduce the bug, what happens and what should happen. First ask for the cause to be identified, then for a limited change and a check of the same steps. Judge the preview or test separately from AI’s claim that the work is done. “When the input is empty, the form displays zero as a valid result. Find the cause, fix only this behaviour and check both empty input and a normal value. Do not publish the change yet.”

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.section: Versioning, Git and GitHub: track every change
documents.text: When making changes, you need to know what changed, why, and which verified state you can return to. A history, labelled releases and a short changelog help.

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.text: A release label, such as 1.4.2 . It tells users which edition they have. A changelog explains fixes, new features and any changes to data handling.

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.text: A tool for tracking project files. It compares changes, records related edits in commits and supports branches. Basic work happens locally on your computer.

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.text: A service for hosting repositories, collaboration and reviewing proposed changes. It can run automated checks or deployments if the project is configured to do so. Git commands · GitHub — pull requests If a project uses Semantic Versioning (SemVer), the numbers describe compatibility of the public interface: PATCH: a compatible fix, for example 1.4.2 → 1.4.3 . MINOR: a new backward-compatible feature, for example 1.4.2 → 1.5.0 . MAJOR: an incompatible public-interface change, for example 1.4.2 → 2.0.0 . 1.5.0-beta.1 denotes a prerelease. Labels such as “work” depend on the project’s own rules. Neither a version number nor the label “final” proves that an application is correct. SemVer specification Commit records selected changes in local history. Push sends them to a remote server. Deployment makes a particular version available to users. A project may deploy automatically after a push or merge into the main branch. Before sending changes, find out what will run. GitHub Actions can, for example, build, test and then publish a release. GitHub — automated checks and deployments Record a verified commit or mark a release with a tag, for example v1.4.2 . A tag names a point in history

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.text: or example, build, test and then publish a release. GitHub — automated checks and deployments Record a verified commit or mark a release with a tag, for example v1.4.2 . A tag names a point in history; the changelog describes changes for users. The command git revert can create a new commit that reverses an earlier change while preserving history. Back up the database, documents and user settings separately. Returning to old code may not restore data changed by a new version. For data-format changes, prepare and test a recovery procedure. Git — release tags Checked 27 October 2026. Further background: Git and GitHub in the official documentation . Do not store passwords, API keys or real private data in the project history.

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.text: Try the same task using your own material. Compare accuracy, corrections needed, waiting time and cost. A model’s name alone does not guarantee a result. In tools offering this option, it adjusts the model’s reasoning effort. A higher setting may help with a complex task but does not guarantee accuracy. Compare the same request at different settings, accounting for time and usage. Official OpenAI documentation — models and reasoning effort Start with an available tool and a specific task. A paid plan may make sense when you hit a limit or need a particular feature. The product’s terms matter. A chat subscription does not automatically pay for a separate API or hosting your application. OpenAI · Claude · Gemini API The chat and API may not offer the same models. Check availability for your account, pricing and any preview designation before deciding. OpenAI · Claude · Gemini

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.text: Extensions meet different needs: repeating a workflow, connecting a service or providing a tool. Start with what your task actually requires. Suppose you want regular summaries of documents. A skill can describe the report format and checks. A connector provides folder access. An MCP server can supply the tools. A plugin may bundle some of these capabilities. The combination depends on the application. Plugin documentation · MCP architecture

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.section: What never to put in an AI chat
documents.text: Before sending a message, file or screenshot, check its contents. These rules apply to ordinary chat fields and attachments; sign in through the service’s designated login or authorisation window.

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.section: Access secrets do not belong in chat
documents.text: Passwords, PINs and login codes: including one-time SMS codes, recovery codes and links that can sign you in or restore access to an account. API keys, tokens and private keys: for example, an AI-service key, GitHub access token, private SSH key or active login cookie. Also check files such as .env and logs. Crypto-wallet recovery phrases: never send a seed phrase or private key to chat, even as a photo. Anyone who obtains them can control the wallet. Payment details that could enable card misuse: full card number, expiry date, CVV/CVC, PIN or payment confirmation codes.

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.text: ID or passport scans, national identification numbers, signatures, exact addresses, personal contacts or photos of children. For ordinary questions, use fictional or substituted details.

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.text: Medical reports, intimate photos, private messages and documents containing other people’s data. Include only a necessary excerpt with identifying details removed.

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.text: Non-public contracts, payslips, statements, client lists and confidential company code. Do not upload these to an ordinary public AI tool without permission; follow your employer’s rules. A paid plan or disabling the use of chats for training does not grant permission to share other people’s data or confidential information. It depends on the service, its settings and the rules applying to the data. Send only what the task needs. Replace names with, for example, [CLIENT A] , account numbers with [ACCOUNT] and access credentials with [REMOVED] . Check the screenshot’s top bar, URL, QR codes and nearby windows too. In documents, consider comments, hidden sheets and metadata. Remove sensitive details or use proper redaction that deletes the content. A black rectangle placed over text in an editable document may leave the original text intact. Inspect the resulting file and check that removed content cannot be read or copied. Replacing a name may not be enough if other details identify the person. ICO — hidden data and safe document redaction . Instead of a full payslip: “Explain gross versus net pay using a fictional example. I do not need a calculation of my actual salary.” Deleting

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.text: person. ICO — hidden data and safe document redaction . Instead of a full payslip: “Explain gross versus net pay using a fictional example. I do not need a calculation of my actual salary.” Deleting the message alone does not secure leaked access. Change the password directly in the original service; revoke an exposed token or API key and replace it. Check signed-in devices and account activity. For work data, inform your administrator; for card details, contact your bank. For a wallet recovery phrase, follow the provider’s official security procedure. Sources checked 27 October 2026: NÚKIB — risks of using AI · NCSC — securing a compromised account · MetaMask — protecting keys and recovery phrases .

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.section: API keys: how to handle them safely
documents.text: An API key lets an application access a service. Misuse of a secret key can mean someone else’s requests are charged to your account. This guidance concerns secret server-side API keys, for example for AI services.

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.text: Use the official account dashboard. Separate development from production and grant only the permissions needed. Use expiry and access restrictions if offered.

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.text: For local development, use an environment variable; in production, use hosting secrets or a secrets manager. Do not place the key in chat, documentation, screenshots or logs.

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.text: The browser sends a request to your server. The server calls the API with the key and returns the response. The visitor never receives the secret key.

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.section: A public page cannot keep a secret key
documents.text: Do not put it in HTML, browser JavaScript or localStorage . Variables such as VITE_… or NEXT_PUBLIC_… may be included in the public build. Hiding or encoding a value does not make it secret. Vite · Next.js . The server endpoint also needs access controls, request limits and input validation, so that anyone cannot use it without limits at your expense. In the server or development environment settings, create a variable named AI_API_KEY . Enter its actual value there, not in the source code. This server-side Python example makes no API calls: The variable name depends on the application. Some libraries expect a specific name, for example OPENAI_API_KEY . A .env file is not automatically loaded in every environment and does not provide encryption by itself. Include local secrets files in .gitignore . A shared .env.example should contain only variable names and empty or obviously invalid values. Review changes before committing; secret scanning can help. Adding a file to .gitignore does not remove a key that has already been committed. A private repository is not a secrets manager either. Regularly review usage and costs in the provider’s dashboard. Separate projects and keys help tra

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.section: A public page cannot keep a secret key
documents.text: ot remove a key that has already been committed. A private repository is not a secrets manager either. Regularly review usage and costs in the provider’s dashboard. Separate projects and keys help trace spending. A budget alert may not stop requests automatically; check the actual limit and how the service enforces it. Immediately revoke the leaked key with the provider. Deleting it from a message or the latest file version is not enough. Create a replacement key, update the application settings and verify that it works. Review usage history, costs and related access. Contact the provider about suspicious activity. Remove the source of the leak. If the secret is in Git history, follow the cleanup documentation and coordinate with others; copies may remain in clones and forks. Checked 27 October 2026: Official OpenAI documentation — key management and production · API authentication · GitHub — removing exposed sensitive data .

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.section: Checking an application after changes and regression testing
documents.text: A regression is a bug where a new change breaks something that used to work. Fixing one button therefore does not mean the whole application has been verified.

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.text: Record the version and original behaviour. For a bug, note the reproduction steps and expected result. Establish the relevant tests’ baseline and protect any data you will use.

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.text: Repeat the original steps and verify the fix. Then check related functions: saving, loading, calculations or export, depending on the change’s scope.

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.text: Review the changed files and verify the build and local preview. After an approved deployment, check the main user flows in the version actually released too. Syntax and build: the code can be processed and the application built. This does not yet verify the result. Unit tests: selected calculations or rules using known inputs. Integration tests: interaction between components, such as importing and saving. User flow: actually entering values, clicking, saving and reloading. Visual checks: mobile and desktop, longer text, error messages and readable controls. Screenshot comparisons can reveal visual changes. Match the scope of checks to the change and its impact. A text correction needs different checks from a change to accounting calculations or a database. Imagine an application that must prevent importing the same items twice. Adding support for a new statement format must preserve that rule. Using test data, import three different transactions and verify that there are three records. Try the same file again. If the application must detect duplicates, the total must still be three records. Check totals, currencies and dates. Also try a previously supported format. Save the data,

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.text: s. Try the same file again. If the application must detect duplicates, the total must still be three records. Check totals, currencies and dates. Also try a previously supported format. Save the data, reopen the application and check the export. Use test or anonymised data. After finding a bug, add a test of the expected behaviour to help catch its return. Smoke test is a quick check of basic flows: the app starts, its main page loads and the key task can be completed. Regression tests guard previously required behaviour during later changes. CI means continuous integration: automated checks can run, for example, when a pull request is created. A green result proves only the checks that actually ran. “First establish and record the baseline. After the fix, check both the original bug and related functions. Use test data. State what you checked, the expected and actual results and anything you could not verify. Do not publish anything yet.” Ask for specific results and unresolved issues. A count of passing tests or “everything works” does not replace checking important user scenarios. Record the steps, version and expected result. Establish whether the issue existed before the chang

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.text: . A count of passing tests or “everything works” does not replace checking important user scenarios. Record the steps, version and expected result. Establish whether the issue existed before the change. Depending on its impact, fix the change or use the prepared rollback; then recheck affected scenarios. Do not overwrite reference screenshots or expected results merely to make a check pass. Sources checked 27 October 2026: Playwright — testing user behaviour · Screenshot comparisons · GitHub Actions and CI .

documents.title: How to work with AI. From a clear request to a result.
documents.text: Choose your own text or two offers, describe the result you want and check what AI returns. You can build on this with a more complex workflow later. More educational content in Czech: AI s rozumem — Filip Oborník . The original explanations on this page are accompanied by links to the vendors’ documentation.

documents.text: I run a browser check and receive a report of loaded pages, errors and places that need attention. Private project. Not publicly available for download. My development tool, run manually. It does not modify the application being checked. Missing evidence is not a pass.

documents.text: Review PASS, WATCH or FAIL with findings and screenshots.

documents.title: Universal App Tester
documents.text: Add another project through configuration rather than a separate tester. My development tool, run manually. It does not modify the application being checked. Missing evidence is not a pass.

documents.title: Universal App Tester
documents.text: I build my own apps — a meal planner, an Italy travel planner, an accounting book, a collection catalogue, … After every change I need to check that all the pages still load normally, nothing throws in the console and nothing is broken. Clicking through it by hand is tedious and easy to miss something. App Tester does it for me. It launches a browser in the background (no window), opens each page of the chosen app one by one and records for each: did it load at all? how fast? are there errors in the browser console? does the page have any content, or is it empty? do the pages differ from each other (does routing work)? From that it composes a clear verdict. Universal = no hardcoding. Apps aren't baked into the code — they live in a simple list (config). Adding a new app means writing a few lines: address, list of pages. The tester is generic, it works on anything that runs in a browser. Same philosophy as the Resident Auditor: never PASS without evidence. When an app isn't running, it gets neither green nor red — it gets „WATCH“ (not enough evidence), so no falsely good result is produced. documents.title: Universal App Tester
documents.text: 6 checks per page — page load, console errors, empty content, load speed, and whether the pages differ from each other (routing works). PASS / WATCH / FAIL verdict — FAIL when something doesn't load or the console throws; WATCH when a page is slow, empty or the app isn't running; PASS only when everything is fine. Universal config — adding an app = one object with a list of pages. No code rewriting. Screenshots + report — a snapshot is saved from each page; the result is a clear per-app report plus a summary across all of them. No false PASS — when an app isn't running it's honestly WATCH, not falsely green. Manual, read-only — no automatic scheduling, it only looks, deploys nothing.

documents.title: Universal App Tester
documents.text: First a self-test (verifies everything is ready), then a test of one app: The tester reports the concrete problem (which page, what error) — not just „something went wrong“.

documents.title: Universal App Tester
documents.text: Version v0.1 (June 2026). Self-test passes (12/12), verified live on a real app. It grew out of earlier one-off scripts, which I unified into a single universal tool controlled the same way as the Resident Auditor.

documents.title: BudLine Panel
documents.text: Why it exists: a bus driver's shifts are scattered across rosters, with weekend and holiday bonuses, and at the end of the month there is a payslip that is hard to verify. BudLine is a simple panel for that: I log my shifts (or read them from the driver card), the app adds them up according to the rules and shows what the pay should be. Two of us use it — me and a colleague from work. Shift and roster records: each shift has a date, times and a type; the app validates the entry (HH:MM time format, no negative numbers) and builds a monthly overview. Payroll documents: from the logged shifts the app calculates the pay basis according to configured rules (hours, bonuses). At the end of the month you just compare it with the payslip — if something is off, you see exactly where. Driver card reading: since version 1.2.13 the app can read data directly from the driver's chip card via a reader — less manual typing. Everything local: data stays on the computer (SQLite). Updates install silently in the background; an upgrade never overwrites user data or settings.

documents.title: BudLine Panel
documents.text: A bus driver gets a payslip every month with a single number on it. Verifying that number means going through the rosters, adding up driving hours, waiting time, night and weekend bonuses and meal allowances — by the collective agreement, not by feel. BudLine Panel does exactly that: it keeps a record of what was actually driven, calculates what should arrive, and puts it next to what really did.

documents.title: BudLine Panel
documents.text: A day comes from two sources. The roster says what was supposed to be driven — trips, times, kilometres, breaks. The DZVA (the daily vehicle operation log) is the dispatcher's paper: document number, bus, tachograph and odometer readings. The app combines both and works out the rest, so you only enter what differs from the plan. Swapping the bus mid-day — just say which route you switched at. Times and kilometres for both vehicles are derived from the roster, and when the counter readings are filled in, actual figures win over the plan. Two shifts in one day — if the dispatcher issues a new DZVA for the afternoon, the day splits into two shifts. Pay is apportioned by driving time; the meal allowance stays whole, because the whole day was spent at work. Extra or dropped trips — the difference in driving time, time at work and kilometres is calculated; duration and distance come from the timetable, nothing is guessed.

documents.title: BudLine Panel
documents.text: On top of the records runs the payroll calculation per the collective agreement: base rate, performance component, waiting time, difficult conditions, night, weekend and holiday bonuses, and the meal allowance by shift length. The result is visible day by day and for the whole month. Monthly pay overview — a day-by-day breakdown: hours worked, how much of that was driving, which bonuses, how many koruna. Months are switched with a picker at the top. Reports — my own payslip and a shift sheet in the same shape as the employer's paper, so they can be compared line by line. Payroll check — item by item against the uploaded payslip, including bonuses and benefits; anything that does not match shows up straight away. Roster check — an indicative estimate of what a given roster will bring, before it is driven.

documents.title: BudLine Panel
documents.text: The app is not supposed to invent figures. When it cannot be sure, it says so and would rather show nothing than show something wrong. An implausible reading is not used — if an odometer reading works out to 50,000 km in a shift, or far beyond the plan, the app treats it as a typo and stays with the plan. It does not pass a typo off as a detour. An empty field says why — whether the value is missing from the DZVA, or only one of the two readings is filled in. A reversed counter (end lower than start) is marked red. The payroll truth stays with the employer's payslip — the app is a checking aid, not a replacement for the payroll office, and it says so on its own outputs. Month close — once a month is closed the figures are locked into a snapshot so they cannot drift. If a roster later turns out to have been different from a certain date, the app offers a recalculation and records why.

documents.title: BudLine Panel
documents.text: Runs locally on Windows (and macOS), no cloud, no account, no telemetry . Data lives on the computer. Backups with a single button, optionally encrypted with a password. A restore can first be tried as a dry run into an isolated copy — you see what the backup contains and live data is never touched. Updates download and install themselves; data and settings are kept. Pages regenerate themselves whenever the data changes — there is nothing to refresh by hand.

documents.title: BudLine Panel
documents.section: What the app does not do
documents.text: It is not a payroll system and it does not replace the payroll office. It does not calculate other people, it sends nothing to the employer and it has no web version. It is one driver's tool for checking his own pay — and it is written that way.

documents.title: BudLine Panel

Work per the DZVA — The daily vehicle operation log next to the plan from the roster. An empty counter says why; a reversed state (end lower than start) is marked red. Shift management — Checking recorded shifts, filling them in from the payslip and closing the month. Recording a shift — Roster and bus from a dropdown. If the vehicle was swapped mid-day, just enter from which route — the rest is worked out; a day can be split into two shifts with their own DZVA. documents.title: Config Center
documents.text: I have about 60 devices at home (lights, motion sensors, TRV heads, speakers, air purifier, blind, …) running on Homey Pro 2026. It can do a lot — has its own mobile app, web UI, scripts, automations — but there are far too many drawers and the settings are scattered. Config Center unifies everything in one place. Open the web in a browser, log in with my token (the token stays only on my PC, nothing is sent anywhere), and see 22 clean pages: one per „house mode“ (morning / day / evening / night / away / home / sleep), separate for heating, lights, audio, etc. Preview mode = safe test. When I want to try something, the app applies it first, gives me 10 minutes to test, and if I don't say „OK, save it“ in that window, it reverts itself. So even if I make a mistake, the house heals itself. Protects from mistakes. Some devices (bedroom audio, sensitive sensors) have a hard-block — they cannot be turned on accidentally. The bedroom speaker can't play a test if someone's sleeping there. Local, mine, no cloud. The app is just an HTML+CSS+JS file opened in Edge or Chrome. It talks directly to the Homey hub at home, nothing goes to a third-party server. No subscription, no vendor cloud dep

documents.title: Energy Dashboard (PC)
documents.text: Why it exists: to know what consumes what. The app shows current draw (W), today's usage (kWh), today's cost , monthly estimate , and which appliance is pulling the most right now (typically fridge, stove, dryer). How it works: at home there's a small server (Raspberry Pi running Home Assistant) collecting data from a 3-phase meter (Shelly Pro 3EM) and individual smart plugs. The app polls it every 30 seconds and redraws. On the PC it runs as a standalone Edge window — no taskbar, no menu, just a dashboard. NT/VT tariff visible: Czech distribution tariff D57D — low tariff (NT, cheap power) at specific hours, high (VT) the rest. A big top badge clearly shows which is active so I can decide whether to run the washer. When RPi is unreachable (e.g. home internet drops), the app shows the last saved data with a clear „cached-stale“ warning. Never shows stale data as if it were live.

documents.title: Energy Dashboard (PC)
documents.text: Real-time consumption — Current draw (W), 3-phase split, top consumer right now. Updates every 30 s. documents.title: Italia Travel Planner
documents.text: Why it exists: Italy travel has its own rules. Historic centers have ZTL zones (Zona Traffico Limitato) — drive in by car and you get an 80–200 € fine. Tickets for the Vatican, Uffizi, and Colosseum sell out a month ahead for specific time slots. Motorhomes need different infrastructure than cars — Stellplatzy, area sosta, dump stations. Mainstream travel apps don't handle this — either they force an account and try to sell everything, or they're Italy-blind. One user, everything local: the app is mine, runs on my computer, on my phone as PWA, or as a Windows desktop app. No backend, no cloud, no API keys. Plans the trip — itinerary, tickets, budget, route. Actual purchases (flights, hotels, tickets) I make myself on official sites — the app just opens them in the browser via deeplink. No contract, no commission, no vendor lock-in. AI Autopilot (since 1.7.0): I answer a few questions — where to, from where, how many days, hotel or sleeping in the car — and Autopilot proposes the whole trip: route, day split, real stops along the route and concrete accommodation for every night. It offers three variants that genuinely differ (hours behind the wheel per day, hotel vs. guesthouse, how

documents.title: Italia Travel Planner
documents.text: trip: route, day split, real stops along the route and concrete accommodation for every night. It offers three variants that genuinely differ (hours behind the wheel per day, hotel vs. guesthouse, how big a detour I tolerate). Every place is real, from OpenStreetMap — with coordinates, address and a visible origin for every number ("from map data" vs. "estimated"); whatever couldn't be found is honestly marked as a wish, not a place. Prices and availability are never invented — map data doesn't have them, so the app doesn't claim them. The proposal can be edited in plain words ("Add a day in Rome"), and before writing into the trip a verified backup is created — if it fails, nothing is overwritten. For car sleeping it searches campsites (not parking lots, which would silently imply sleeping is allowed) and proposes a backup overnight spot in case the first one is full. Planning from scratch: New trip (name, region, dates, party size, budget, style — city / roadtrip / coast / mountains / wine & food / camper). documents.title: Meal Planner
documents.text: Why it exists: I tried several mainstream diet apps (MyFitnessPal, Yazio, Lifesum…) and they all annoyed me. Either they wanted an account and pushed ads, or didn't know Czech meals, or forced a specific nutrition ideology. This one runs only in my browser — profile lives in localStorage, no server sees my weight, calories, or what I'm eating today. How it works: I enter my height, weight, age, activity. The app computes my daily calorie need (Mifflin-St Jeor for resting metabolism + activity multiplier). For weight loss it recommends an asymmetric deficit. For muscle gain it also prioritizes higher-protein recipes. Weekly meal-box plan: The app searches a database of ~21 recipes and builds 7 days × 5 meals (breakfast, snack, lunch, snack, dinner) so the daily kcal lands within ±10% of target. Then it generates a shopping list — sums all ingredients for the week and groups them by category. Export to CSV or print. Optional Rohlík: If I'm a Rohlík customer, I can have an agent (Claude) prepare a cart proposal from the weekly plan, paste JSON into Settings and see the cart preview with totals vs minimum vs delivery price. The order is always confirmed manually in Rohlík UI — the app

documents.text: prepare a cart proposal from the weekly plan, paste JSON into Settings and see the cart preview with totals vs minimum vs delivery price. The order is always confirmed manually in Rohlík UI — the app physically cannot order or pay (5-layer defense-in-depth). PWA = works offline: After first load it caches and works without internet. documents.text: 1.0.2 — faster saving with database mirroring switched on (October 2026) — the first release since 1.0.1 that actually brings something. In Settings you can switch on mirroring of your data to a local database; with it on, the app rewrote everything on every save, including what had not changed. With a full fridge of images that meant megabytes just to add one item, and you could feel it. Now only what I actually changed is sent. Deletions reach the mirror as reliably as before — I checked that separately, because it is exactly where it is easy to slip and bring back something you had deleted. If you do not have mirroring on (the default), you will notice no difference. Under the hood: the helper code for storage access had been copied five times across different files, and now lives in one place. 1080 unit tests, e2e 76/76. A note for honesty: on the first test run one performance test (the plan generator) exceeded its time limit and failed; it was not a regression — the generator code did not change at all, the test passed in isolation and the second full run came out 1080/1080. documents.title: Home Media Hub
documents.text: My home NAS is full of movies, series, music and home videos — but clicking through network folders to find them is no fun. Media Hub is a light, nice front-end over it: it shows the library as tiles, lets me search and filter by type, mark items as "seen" and "favourite" — and runs right next to the TV on a small Raspberry Pi. Read-only, nothing gets broken. The dashboard treats the media on the NAS strictly read-only — it only browses them (no deleting, moving or overwriting). The "seen/favourite" flags and the index live in its own local database (SQLite), never on the NAS. Safe import from disk to NAS. When I find an old external disk with scattered media, Media Hub first only scans it, sorts files by type (movies, series, music, photos, home videos, documents) and shows a plan preview . Only after I confirm does it copy — and only new files: the source is never deleted, nothing on the NAS is overwritten, and every copy is verified. The order is always scan → proposal → preview → confirm → copy → verify . Artwork and descriptions from Jellyfin. Optionally it connects to my home Jellyfin (running on the NAS) and adds posters, genre, length and description to films — still read-o

documents.title: Portfolio Tracker
documents.text: I use Bookkeeping for the overall financial picture and Portfolio Tracker to follow investments over time. The former Finance Analytik is now part of PT, bringing portfolio tracking and stock analysis together in one app. Transactions are the source of truth. Instead of typing "I own 10 shares", the app keeps individual buys, sells and dividends — and derives positions, average price and realized gain from them (FIFO). That keeps taxes and history consistent. It reads broker statements itself. Drop in a CSV / XLSX / PDF from XTB, eToro, Trading 212 or Interactive Brokers; the app detects the broker, normalizes the format and de-duplicates repeated imports (a fingerprint per transaction). XTB accounts can be split by currency (USD/EUR/CZK separately). Taxes by Czech rules. FIFO matching of sales, the 3-year time test (exemption for long holding) and the §4 value test (sale proceeds ≤ CZK 100,000/year). The summary is always computed in CZK even when the portfolio base is e.g. USD (converted at the historical rate on the trade date). Performance and fair value. documents.title: Smart Home Resident Auditor
documents.text: My home is run by lots of automations — lights, audio, heating, blinds, scenes. Ordinary tools only report „the script finished without error“. But a technically successful script doesn't mean it was pleasant for a human. The radio might start three times in a row, a light might switch on at full brightness at night, the heating might run while nobody is home — and all of it „technically ran OK“. Resident Auditor looks differently. It takes the stored logs of the home for a specific day and asks, in human terms: Was the morning calm? Did the lights react to movement and did the blinds take priority? Did anything stay on or keep playing after I left? Did the heating behave sensibly? Did anything wake me at night? The key rule: never PASS without evidence. If there's no proof something went well, it doesn't get a green light — it gets „WATCH“. And the reverse too: routine, harmless events don't count as a problem, so there are no false alarms . The goal is a trustworthy verdict, not pretty statistics. It changes nothing. The tool is strictly read-only — it only reads logs. It never touches the home, fixes nothing, and doesn't run in the background. I launch it manually when I want to

documents.title: Smart Home Resident Auditor
documents.text: 10 areas of daily life — morning, night movement, audio & voice messages, lights & blinds, bathroom, heating, device reliability and system stability. Each has its own „auditor“. Evidence-based verdict: PASS / WATCH / FAIL — green only with positive proof of correct behaviour; otherwise watch; red only for a real problem. No false PASS and no false alarm — it tells a real action apart from a routine check, so it doesn't flag a problem where there is none. A suggested next step for every problem — when something fails, a „task to solve“ is created with evidence (time, what happened, impact on the resident) — but a fix never runs on its own, it waits for my decision. Audit of a specific day — I run it for a chosen day and get a clear report; ideal as a check after every change to the home. Manual, safe — no automatic scheduling, no interference with the home, read-only.

documents.title: Home wall panel
documents.text: Why it exists: phone control of a smart home is fast only relative to how slow it is. By the time you unlock the phone, find the app, tap the right icon, scroll — you could've just turned the lights on by hand. A wall panel solves this exactly. Always on, always ready, everything important on the first screen. Hardware: Raspberry Pi 4 (small computer the size of a deck of cards) + 7" touch display, screwed to the hallway wall. About €100 total. Lives in a Chromium browser launched in „kiosk mode“ — no OS UI, no menu, just the full-window app. What it does: control all lights, start/stop radio, switch scene (relax / cinema / cooking / dinner / arriving / leaving), adjust heating, see what the house is consuming in real time, who's home, who's asleep, where motion was last detected. Scenes Loxone-style: big tiles, tap „Cinema“ with a thumb and the whole flat reconfigures — lights to 30%, music quietens, blind blocks the street, heating up one degree. One touch instead of ten.

documents.title: Collection — Numismatics & Philately
documents.text: Why it exists: a friend from work collects coins and stamps as a hobby and kept asking me questions — what is this piece, where do I look it up, what does it sell for. So I built him an app to make it clear: photograph the item, the app helps identify it and give an indicative valuation , and links straight to places where the price can be verified. Runs locally, looks like an auction-house catalogue, no account, no data leaves the machine. Two modes: a public demo (sample data only, runs in the browser) and the full version on my PC with its own database, photos and AI. The real collection never leaves the computer. AI recognition from a photo: photograph a coin or stamp, the app sends the photo to AI (Gemini) which reads the text on the item and pre-fills the form — category, country, year, denomination, condition. Then you just review and save. It handles both sides at once (obverse + reverse). If the photo is blurry or it is not a coin, the app fills nothing and asks for a new photo (like document verification). Where it sells: I browse catalogues and shops (Numista, Pofis, Colnect, Delcampe…) right inside the app — each result shows the name, price and image, and prices in for

documents.title: Collection — Numismatics & Philately
documents.text: o (like document verification). Where it sells: I browse catalogues and shops (Numista, Pofis, Colnect, Delcampe…) right inside the app — each result shows the name, price and image, and prices in foreign currencies are converted to Czech koruna using the Czech National Bank rate. Each item also keeps a price history over time, so I can see where the value is heading. You see immediately what the same item actually sells for — not what someone is asking. Help for beginners: a dedicated page explains the AI (Gemini) in plain language — how to get a free key and what it costs — plus shooting with a phone, backups and security. The AI key can be entered right in the app and stays only on the computer. What drives the price: an educational section — what raises value (higher grade, mint errors, certification, NH gum on stamps) and what lowers it (cleaning, mounting holes, defects). So you never buy or sell blind. Bulk import: if you already keep a list in Excel, upload it in one go (CSV / XLSX) instead of clicking item by item.

documents.title: TenisPark
documents.text: Why it exists: anyone who looks after a few tennis courts with a kiosk knows it: bookings in one notebook, "on the tab" (who drank what and hasn't paid) in another, counting the till on a calculator in the evening and personal money in a third one. TenisPark joins it all into one app that absolutely anyone can use — every page has an expandable "how to" help. Tennis courts: bookings take a few clicks — court, from–to, name. The app won't allow two people on the same court at the same time, the price is pre-filled from the price list (different for weekdays and weekends), and after payment you click "Paid". Plus maintenance records (lining, watering) and occupancy and revenue reports per day and month. Kiosk: sales with a stock that watches itself — you can't sell more than is in stock, and the app warns when something is running low. A special feature is the debtors book : whoever doesn't pay right away gets their consumption written "on the tab" with their name, and whoever doesn't pay within 3 days lights up red. In the evening you run the daily closing — the app compares how much should be in the till with what's really there. When prices change, the old price stays visible cros

documents.text: y within 3 days lights up red. In the evening you run the daily closing — the app compares how much should be in the till with what's really there. When prices change, the old price stays visible crossed out next to the new one. Home budget: personal income and expenses like receipts, categories (envelopes), monthly limits "how much I want to spend on food", plus a year-round planning section for seasonal work — how much to put aside in summer so winter works out. Everything local and safe: data lives in an SQLite database on your PC only, backs up with one click to a file with a checksum, and a restore always shows a preview first. The app has a light and dark look in clay-court colours.

documents.title: Finance — Ledger
documents.text: I built it because I got tired of switching between online banking, broker websites and Excel. The app handles 25 different sources — bank and payment accounts, brokers including an options broker, crypto exchanges and wallets, P2P platforms, precious metals and pension savings. Instead of logging in to every platform, one page shows assets, cash, investments, debts and net worth — and for every number the app can show which rows it came from. It finds its own work. Documents that are not in the book yet it finds by itself in watched folders and in my mailbox (a small watcher on a Raspberry Pi pulls attachments from Gmail and from a second mailbox, and is set up directly in the app; the documents are then fetched onto every computer running the app). What is unambiguous it posts; what is not, it hands to me with a plain sentence saying why it left it alone. Twice a day it recalculates overviews, aligns account names and currencies with the statements, applies an extra loan repayment to the principal and clears the queue of rows waiting for a decision. If I start it after a week, it catches up on missed runs right after start. Nothing is estimated. An account balance is a documented

documents.title: Finance — Ledger
documents.text: the principal and clears the queue of rows waiting for a decision. If I start it after a week, it catches up on missed runs right after start. Nothing is estimated. An account balance is a documented figure from the statement, not a sum of movements. An exchange rate is the Czech National Bank rate for that date. Every tax rule carries its paragraph, official source and verification date — a historical transaction is judged by the law of its own year. Where a document is missing or the law gives no answer, the app refuses to produce a number and says why. Every important calculation has an independent “shadow” recomputation watching over it. No cloud, no data leaving. The database is a single SQLite file on my Windows machine. A full backup carries the whole system (database, documents, settings) and, if it includes API keys, it is always encrypted (AES-256-GCM). The book stays on the local computer; the home NAS is used only for silent updates (verified by checksum) and for a one-way backup that is always stored encrypted.

documents.text: The app has 14 modules in the main menu and around 150 screens. This is a selection of what I use most. Overview — assets, cash, investments and net worth on one page; charts of portfolio and net-worth development for 1 year, 2 years or the whole period, portfolio allocation with a “where and how much” breakdown on click, emergency-reserve and limit tiles, a freshness traffic light for statements (which account is missing a statement and since when), loan coverage by crypto value, cash-flow outlook and financial independence. Imports — 25 sources without touching code — bank statements (PDF, CSV and API), payment accounts, XTB, eToro, Trading 212, Interactive Brokers, an options broker, crypto exchanges plus hardware and software wallets, P2P platforms, precious metals, pension savings, payslips. The wizard tells you exactly which export to download. A bank statement is verified against itself before posting (opening balance + movements = closing balance) and a statement that does not add up is rejected as a whole. documents.text: an old row propagates by itself to every affected domain (impact graph, 13 domains in fixed order); the whole book is never recalculated needlessly. System: health, engines, operations — “What is missing” with one of six verbs (Add, Sync, Import, Pair, Check, Fix); 20 application engines with a human-readable state and a link to where it gets resolved (an unmeasured engine never pretends to be fine); reconciliation that modules agree with each other to the cent; operation history and recovery of an unfinished recalculation; incident diagnostics with a problem fingerprint instead of a white screen. Backup, transfer and uninstall — full backup of the whole system in parts with verification, automatic encrypted backup to the home NAS (one-way, restore is manual), API keys transferred only in an encrypted envelope, restore by chunked upload with preview, complete uninstall including data (external backups are never deleted). Silent updates from the home NAS with SHA-256 checksum. Quick search Ctrl+K — finds 130+ pages without diacritics and even by path; destructive actions cannot even be written into the palette.

documents.title: Finance — Ledger
documents.text: Working beta v0.10.118 (22 October 2026). Local Windows app, ~10 months of active development, silent updates from the home NAS. The last full release gate (v0.10.35) passed with more than 16,000 automated tests (backend 10,844, tools 1,803, frontend 3,970); newer releases go through targeted tests, an install test, a SHA-256 fingerprint check and a smoke test over an isolated copy of the book (most recently 149 checks, the whole frontend of 4,117 tests with no failures) and an independent verifier for every larger task. Private — no public hosting, no third-party API.

documents.title: Naples & Amalfi Coast
documents.text: September 2023 — 82 photos in 6 sections. Naples, Pompeii, Vesuvius, the Amalfi coast, Positano. Loud, chaotic, authentic. The Italy you don't see from a tour bus window.

documents.title: Naples & Amalfi Coast
documents.text: Southern Italy is loud, chaotic, beautiful. Naples has Spaccanapoli — narrow streets where life happens on the street, not behind closed doors. Pompeii makes 79 AD feel like yesterday. The Amalfi Coast bends along cliffs so steep that driving feels like flying. Difference from the north: traffic is wild, but the welcome is real. Order a "caffè" at any bar and you'll feel at home in 30 seconds.

documents.title: Naples & Amalfi Coast
documents.text: My full Pompeii video ↗ and photographs show the archaeological city. Give it its own time alongside Naples and the coast. The archaeological park publishes current ticket types, opening and last-entry times and visitor rules; these can change with the season. Before setting out: check which part of the site your ticket covers, the entrance you plan to use and current access to individual buildings. The park also provides details of the more accessible “Pompeii for All” route. I leave prices and hours to its live information. Tickets and visiting information — Pompeii Sites ↗

documents.title: Italy on a plate
documents.text: Photos from my home kitchen, verified traditional recipes, a pasta guide and notes on regional differences. Personal experience backed by Italian sources — not the one truth, but an honest foundation. Updated: May 2026 · Photos from spring 2020 lockdown · Home cooking in CZ from Italian sources Who this page is for: anyone who loves Italian food and wants to know what the honest version of the classics looks like — no cream in carbonara, no pineapple on pizza, no universal "Italian" sauces. 9 recipes from my kitchen, a guide to 13 pasta types, and notes on what eating in Italy actually means. What you won't find here: "10-minute quick recipes", marketing food porn, attempts at a single truth. Italian cuisine is regional — I respect that.

documents.title: Italy on a plate
documents.text: Italian cooking is strongly regional. Carbonara from Rome, ragù from Bologna, pesto from Genoa or risotto from Milan — each region has its own ingredients, rules and family variations. The goal of this page isn't to claim the one truth , but to show an honest foundation. Italian cuisine may vary by region, town or family tradition. I present recipes as a verified traditional version from a specific source, not as the only existing possibility.

documents.title: Italy on a plate
documents.text: Personal experience — from my stay in Italy (Lerici, Liguria), from time spent with Italians and from traveling through different regions. Verified Italian sources — Italia.it, Accademia Italiana della Cucina, official regional tourism sites, DOP/IGP/STG consortia. Italian YouTube cooking channels — GialloZafferano and CookAround as audiovisual supplement, not as sole proof of tradition. Regional differences — where a recipe exists in multiple variants, it's clearly labeled.

documents.title: Italy on a plate
documents.text: A Roman classic: spaghetti in a creamy sauce of egg yolks, pecorino and rendered guanciale fat. No cream — pasta water helps bring the sauce together. Quantities from the GialloZafferano video. Tick off ingredients as you prepare them. 160 g spaghetti 75 g guanciale 3 medium egg yolks 25 g finely grated pecorino romano Black pepper to taste Salt for the pasta water Cut the guanciale into strips and grate the pecorino. Bring water to the boil; salt lightly, as the pork and cheese are salty. Cook the guanciale in a dry pan over medium heat until golden and the fat has rendered. Lift out the pieces, leaving the fat in the pan. Cook the spaghetti al dente according to the packet. Reserve a cup of cooking water before draining. Mix the yolks, pecorino and freshly ground pepper in a bowl. Toss the pasta in the rendered fat. Remove the pan from the heat, let it cool briefly, then stir in the yolk mixture. Add reserved water a spoonful at a time until creamy. Return the guanciale, toss and serve immediately. Do not boil the sauce after adding the yolks, or the eggs will scramble. Regional note: the traditional Roman version uses no onion or garlic. Northern variants sometimes include pance

Northern variants sometimes include pancetta but in Rome that's considered a swap. Cook and practise listening to Italian: listen for tuorli (yolks), mescolare (to stir) and a fuoco spento (with the heat off). Spaghetti all'amatriciana · Lazio / Amatrice

documents.title: Italy on a plate
documents.text: An Amatrice speciality with guanciale, tomatoes and pecorino , without onion or garlic. This is the GialloZafferano video version with white wine and chilli. Quantities from the GialloZafferano video. Tick off ingredients as you prepare them. 160 g spaghetti 200 g peeled tomatoes 75 g guanciale 37.5 g finely grated pecorino romano 25 g dry white wine ½ fresh chilli (adjust to its heat) Olive oil as needed Salt to taste Cut the guanciale into strips, grate the pecorino and crush the peeled tomatoes. Prepare the chilli; remove its seeds for a milder sauce. Brown the guanciale over medium heat. Add a little olive oil if needed. Pour in the white wine and let it reduce briefly. Lift out the guanciale, leaving the fat and juices in the pan. Add the tomatoes and chilli. Simmer for about 10–15 minutes until thickened. Salt to taste, remembering that the cheese and pork are salty. Cook the spaghetti al dente according to the packet. Reserve a cup of cooking water before draining. Return the guanciale to the sauce and toss in the pasta. Remove from the heat, add the pecorino and toss. Loosen with reserved pasta water, a spoonful at a time, if needed. Serve immediately. documents.title: Italy on a plate
documents.text: Wide egg tagliatelle with slow-cooked meat ragù . This version follows the GialloZafferano video with pancetta and red wine; pasta quantities are added for a complete dish. Ragù based on the video, with 80 g dried tagliatelle per person added. Measure wine in ml. Allow at least 2 hours for simmering. Tick off prepared ingredients. 160 g dried egg tagliatelle 150 g minced beef 75 g pancetta 150 g tomato passata 25 g carrot 25 g celery 25 g onion 50 ml dry red wine ½ tbsp olive oil Hot vegetable stock as needed Salt and black pepper to taste Finely chop the carrot, celery and onion. Cut the pancetta into small pieces. Cook the pancetta in the oil, add the vegetables and soften over low heat. Add the beef and brown it, breaking up any lumps. Add the red wine and let it reduce. Stir in the passata and a little hot stock. Simmer gently for at least 2 hours, stirring occasionally. Add a little stock if it dries out. Finish with a thick sauce; season with salt and pepper. Cook the tagliatelle in salted water according to the packet. Reserve a cup of cooking water before draining. Toss the tagliatelle with the ragù. If too thick, loosen with pasta water a spoonful at a time and serve immed

documents.text: in salted water according to the packet. Reserve a cup of cooking water before draining. Toss the tagliatelle with the ragù. If too thick, loosen with pasta water a spoonful at a time and serve immediately. You can also serve the ragù with pappardelle. These quantities are for dried tagliatelle; fresh pasta needs different portion sizes and cooking times. Italian listening: tritare (chop), rosolare (brown), a fuoco basso (over low heat). The video makes the ragù, not the pasta itself. Gnocchi al pesto alla genovese · Liguria / Genova

documents.title: Italy on a plate
documents.text: Potato gnocchi with basil pesto, pine nuts and two cheeses. The video shows how to make the pesto ; here we pair it with ready-made gnocchi. Pesto proportions from the video, with 200 g ready-made gnocchi per person added. For 2 servings, use half the video's batch of pesto. Tick off prepared ingredients. 400 g ready-made potato gnocchi 35 g fresh basil leaves 35 g extra virgin olive oil 25 g finely grated parmigiano reggiano 15 g finely grated pecorino sardo 15 g pine nuts 1 garlic clove 1.5 g coarse salt for the pesto Salt for the water to taste Rinse the basil gently and dry thoroughly without crushing it. Grate both cheeses and peel the garlic. Crush the garlic with salt in a mortar, then work in the basil and pine nuts. Gradually mix in the cheeses and oil. If using a blender, pulse briefly to keep the pesto cool. Cook the gnocchi in salted water according to the packet. Reserve a little cooking water before lifting them out. Put the pesto in a bowl and loosen with a little lukewarm cooking water. Fold in the gnocchi and serve immediately. Do not boil or fry the pesto. Keep the pesto cool. Use short pulses in a blender; traditionally the ingredients are crushed in a mortar. It

Use short pulses in a blender; traditionally the ingredients are crushed in a mortar. Italian listening: basilico (basil), pinoli (pine nuts), mortaio (mortar). The video shows pesto; cook the gnocchi according to the packet. Risotto alla milanese · Lombardia / Milano

documents.title: Italy on a plate
documents.text: Creamy saffron risotto following the Boeucc restaurant version in the video. This version uses meat stock and butter, without added marrow . Quantities for the Boeucc version in the video, without added marrow. Butter for the base and for finishing is listed separately. Tick off prepared ingredients. 160 g Carnaroli rice 0.125 g saffron threads 75 g dry white wine ¼ white onion 12.5 g butter for the onion 60 g cold butter to finish 40 g finely grated parmigiano reggiano Hot meat stock as needed Salt to taste Steep the saffron in a little warm stock for at least 30 minutes. Keep the remaining stock hot. Finely chop the onion. Soften the onion in the butter for the base. Add the rice and toast briefly, stirring constantly. Add the wine and let it reduce. Add hot stock a ladle at a time, letting each addition absorb before the next. Stir regularly. During cooking, add the saffron and its liquid. Cook for about 16–18 minutes, depending on the rice, until al dente. Add stock as needed. Remove from the heat and stir in the cold finishing butter and parmigiano. Season, rest for 1–2 minutes and loosen with stock if needed; it should spread gently on the plate. Regional note: in Lombardy se

Regional note: in Lombardy served "all'onda" — liquid but not soup. Plated flat on the plate. documents.title: Italy on a plate
documents.text: Simple summer risotto with tomatoes. Not a classified regional specialty but part of home cuisine across Italy. Onion, tomato passata and grana padano. Quantities from the GialloZafferano video. Adjust stock to the rice's absorption. Tick off prepared ingredients. 160 g Carnaroli rice 275 g tomato passata 300 g vegetable stock; more if needed 30 g white onion 5 basil leaves 25 g finely grated grana padano 25 g cold butter Olive oil and salt as needed Heat the stock and keep it hot. Finely chop the onion and soften in a little olive oil. Add the rice and toast briefly while stirring. Stir in the passata and a ladle of hot stock. Cook over low to medium heat, stirring and adding stock a ladle at a time. Taste after about 16–18 minutes, depending on the rice; the grains should be al dente. Remove from the heat and stir in the cold butter, grana padano and torn basil. Season with salt. Rest for 1–2 minutes. If too thick, loosen with a little hot stock and serve immediately. Regional note: variations with mozzarella or pancetta in different regions. Italian listening: riso (rice), passata (strained tomatoes), tostare (toast). Spaghetti al pomodoro · all Italy

documents.text: variations with mozzarella or pancetta in different regions. Italian listening: riso (rice), passata (strained tomatoes), tostare (toast). Spaghetti al pomodoro · all Italy

documents.title: Italy on a plate
documents.text: Simple spaghetti with tomato sauce, basil and olive oil gently flavoured with garlic. Good tomatoes and a gentle simmer make the sauce. Quantities from the GialloZafferano video. Tick off prepared ingredients. 160 g spaghetti 400 g peeled tomatoes 15 g extra virgin olive oil ½ garlic clove Fresh basil and salt to taste Peel the garlic and crush the tomatoes. Gently warm the oil with the garlic in a pan; do not let it brown. Add the tomatoes, season lightly and simmer for about 30 minutes. Stir occasionally and add a little water if needed. Remove the garlic and add torn basil. Cook the spaghetti al dente according to the packet, reserving a cup of cooking water before draining. Toss the spaghetti in the sauce. Add pasta water a spoonful at a time if needed, adjust the seasoning and serve immediately. Regional note: in the south (Campania, Sicily) no cheese. In the north occasionally parmigiano or pecorino added. Italian listening: aglio (garlic), basilico (basil), scolare (drain). Penne al pomodoro / arrabbiata · all Italy

documents.title: Italy on a plate
documents.text: Penne with tomato sauce. If with chili, it becomes penne all'arrabbiata (Lazio). Penne (rigate) shape holds the sauce in its grooves. Quantities from the all’arrabbiata video. Omit chilli for mild penne al pomodoro, or adjust it to its heat. Tick off prepared ingredients. 160 g penne rigate 190 g drained peeled tomatoes ½ garlic clove 1½ small dried chillies (optional) Parsley, olive oil and salt to taste Crush the drained tomatoes. Peel the garlic, chop the parsley and crumble the chilli if using. Gently warm a little oil with the garlic and chilli. Do not brown the garlic. Add the tomatoes and salt lightly. Simmer the sauce for about 12–15 minutes, stirring occasionally. Meanwhile cook the penne al dente and reserve a little cooking water. Remove the garlic, add the penne and toss. Loosen with a little pasta water if needed. Finish with parsley and serve. Regional note: arrabbiata means "angry" — because of chili. Roman classic. Italian listening: peperoncino (chilli), prezzemolo (parsley), piccante (spicy). The video shows the spicy version. Penne alla panna · Northern Italy

documents.title: Italy on a plate
documents.text: Creamy pasta from northern Italy (Lombardy, Piedmont, Veneto). Often with ham (prosciutto cotto) or mushrooms. Watch out: cream in carbonara = mistake, but in penne alla panna = legitimate. The version with ham from the GialloZafferano video. Tick off prepared ingredients. 160 g penne rigate 100 g cooked ham (prosciutto cotto) 125 g liquid whipping cream 25 g finely grated parmigiano reggiano ½ garlic clove Parsley and olive oil as needed Salt, black pepper and a pinch of nutmeg Cut the ham into pieces, grate the parmigiano and chop the parsley. Start cooking the penne in salted water according to the packet. Gently warm the garlic in a little oil, add the ham and cook briefly. Remove the garlic. Add the cream, pepper and a pinch of nutmeg. Let it thicken briefly over low heat without reducing it too far. Reserve a cup of pasta water before draining. Toss the al dente penne with the sauce, adding a little reserved water if needed. Remove from the heat and stir in the parmigiano and parsley. Taste, adjust the salt and serve immediately. Regional note: this is the north's answer to roman carbonara. Different region, different rules. Italian listening: panna (cream), prosciutto cotto

documents.title: Italy on a plate
documents.section: 🌾 Italian pasta types and what they suit
documents.text: 13 main shapes you'll encounter. Each is paired with sauces it best holds. Spaghetti — long thin. Tomato sauces, carbonara, aglio e olio. Spaghettoni — thicker spaghetti. Heavier sauces. Linguine — flat ribbons. Seafood, pesto. Fettuccine / Tagliatelle — wide egg ribbons. Ragù, butter sauces. Pappardelle — wide ribbons. Hearty meat ragùs (wild boar, hare). Penne (rigate) — diagonally cut tubes with ridges. Tomato sauces, arrabbiata. Rigatoni — wide ridged tubes. Carbonara north variant, amatriciana. Fusilli — corkscrews. Cold pasta salads, pesto. Farfalle — bow ties. Cream sauces, salads. Orecchiette — "little ears". Apulian classic with broccoli rabe. Bucatini — spaghetti with a hole. Amatriciana. Conchiglie — shells. Holds chunky sauces. Gnocchi — potato dumplings. Pesto, butter and sage, light tomato. Rule of thumb: thin pasta with light sauces, thick/ridged pasta with heavy sauces.

documents.title: Italy on a plate
documents.section: 🌾 How to recognize good pasta and honest ingredients
documents.text: Bronze-die pasta (trafilata al bronzo) — rougher surface holds sauce. Look for "trafilata al bronzo" on the label. Slow drying at low temp — better starch structure. Premium brands list "essiccata lentamente". Italian wheat — "grano italiano" matters for some. Most pasta uses imported wheat (Canada, Australia) — not necessarily worse. DOP/IGP marks — guarantee of origin and method. Examples: Pasta di Gragnano IGP, Pomodoro San Marzano DOP, Pesto Genovese, Parmigiano Reggiano DOP. Olive oil — extra virgin (EVOO), cold pressed, "Italian" not "bottled in Italy". Check origin on label. Cheese: parmigiano reggiano (cow, north), pecorino romano (sheep, Lazio), grana padano (cow, milder). Each has specific use.

documents.title: Italy on a plate
documents.text: Carbonara has cream. No. Egg, pecorino, guanciale fat, pasta water = creaminess. Spaghetti bolognese is Italian. No. Bolognese ragù goes on tagliatelle. Spaghetti bolognese is a British-American invention. Pesto must be made in a blender. No. Traditional pesto is made in a marble mortar with wooden pestle. Blender heats the oil and oxidizes the basil. Italians eat pizza with knife and fork everywhere. Depends. Restaurant pizza, especially Neapolitan, often eaten with hands (folded "a libretto"). Knife/fork in formal settings. Pineapple on pizza is a global thing. No. In Italy "Hawaiian" pizza is considered an insult to pizza culture. Don't order it there. Pasta cooked al dente means undercooked. No. Al dente means firm to the bite, not raw. Cooking pasta soft = mushy, sauce won't stick. Garlic is in every Italian recipe. No. Many classics use no garlic (carbonara, amatriciana, alfredo). South uses more garlic than north. Parmesan on everything. No. Never on seafood pasta. Never on fish. The fundamental rule of Italian cooking.

documents.title: Italy on a plate
documents.text: Brief overview of regional cuisine characters: North (Lombardia, Piemonte, Veneto): butter, cream, polenta, risotto, ossobuco, gorgonzola. Center (Toscana, Lazio, Umbria): olive oil, beans, bread soup (ribollita), wild game, pecorino. South (Campania, Calabria, Puglia): tomato base, seafood, mozzarella di bufala, chili, dried pasta. Islands (Sicilia, Sardegna): seafood, citrus, sweet/savory mix (pasta alla Norma, arancini, pane carasau). Mountains (Trentino, Friuli): Austrian/Slovenian influences. Speck, knödel, sauerkraut variants. The further south, the more tomatoes, olive oil and chili. The further north, the more butter, rice and meat broths.

documents.title: Practical guide to Italy
documents.text: Sources checked 27 October 2026. Statistics are labelled with the year they cover. The mafia is not a single organisation. Different criminal structures use intimidation, extortion, corruption and money laundering. Their influence can extend into seemingly ordinary businesses. INTERPOL — organised crime in Italy .

documents.title: Practical guide to Italy
documents.text: Cosa Nostra: historically associated with Sicily. ’Ndrangheta: originates in Calabria; its networks also operate outside Italy. Camorra: associated with Campania and Naples, comprising different clans. Sacra Corona Unita and other Apulian groups: Apulia does not have just one organisation. DIA also distinguishes groups from Foggia and Bari; Sacra Corona Unita is associated mainly with Salento. These are areas of origin and historical activity, not limits to their operations or labels for local residents. DIA — 2024 report, in English (PDF) .

documents.title: Practical guide to Italy
documents.text: Alongside drug trafficking, activities include extortion, laundering proceeds and infiltrating the economy. Investigations have also documented corruption of officials and interference in elections and public procurement. One example is the 2023 international operation against an ’Ndrangheta network; a specific case cannot automatically be applied to every business in the region. Europol — a case in Calabria .

documents.title: Practical guide to Italy
documents.text: Direzione Investigativa Antimafia (DIA) coordinates investigations into mafia structures. Action against their assets is also important. The report for 2024 , presented in May 2025, records 53 completed investigative operations and 309 measures restricting personal liberty. These are not statistics for 2026. Ministry of the Interior — DIA results for 2024 . Prevention also protects public investment from infiltration. In July 2026, the Ministry of the Interior published information on the relevant unit’s activities through 30 June 2026. Ministry of the Interior — prevention in 2026 .

documents.title: Practical guide to Italy
documents.text: Menu prices, a restaurant’s appearance or staff greetings do not reveal mafia links. A business or person cannot be labelled this way without evidence. Reports of organised crime are not safety assessments of every street or tourist route.

documents.text: Checked as of 27 October 2026. Amounts apply to specific places and offences; seasonal rules must be checked for the year of your visit.

documents.title: Practical guide to Italy
documents.section: At the table and when greeting people
documents.text: Customs are not laws: cappuccino is typical at breakfast, but you can order it later. Cheese is not usually added to fish pasta, though recipes vary. Spaghetti is usually eaten with a fork; in informal settings, using bread to finish the sauce (fare la scarpetta) is fine. Coperto is not a tip and is not the same as servizio. Check surcharges and service charges on the menu. In Lazio, including Rome, charging coperto is prohibited; listing it on the menu does not make it legal. Regional law, Article 77 . Tipping is optional, with no mandatory percentage. Buongiorno, buonasera and salve are polite choices; ciao is informal, not forbidden in shops.

documents.title: Practical guide to Italy
documents.text: At St Peter’s Basilica, everyone must cover their shoulders. Men should wear long trousers; women should wear trousers or a skirt below the knee. Shorts and miniskirts are not allowed. Check the individual visitor rules at other sites. Basilica rules . Dress when leaving the beach. Restrictions on swimwear or bare torsos are local, not uniform across Italy. The relevant municipal ordinance and its geographical and time limits apply.

documents.title: Practical guide to Italy
documents.text: Sardinia: removing sand, pebbles or shells is prohibited (€500–3,000). Walking on dunes or driving onto beaches: €100–1,000. Regional rules . La Pelosa: the official portal for the 2026 season listed bookings from 15 May to 15 October and entry with a QR code. That period has ended. Check dates, prices, children’s rules and required equipment for the next season on the official booking website ; the 2026 conditions do not automatically apply to 2027. The portal also warns about fake booking sites. Capri: do not assume every beach requires a booking. Before travelling, check the chosen beach’s rules and current municipal ordinances , particularly seasonal traffic restrictions.

documents.title: Practical guide to Italy
documents.text: ZTL: restrictions depend on the zone, time and vehicle category. Navigation directions or a hotel booking are not entry permits. Agree the authorised route and plate-registration procedure with your accommodation in advance; this does not automatically cover other zones or reserved lanes. Example: Florence . The penalty depends on the specific offence. Florence — Scudo Verde: an emissions restriction covering a wider area than the historic ZTL. The municipal tourism portal states that, since 1 July 2025, it covers Euro 0 petrol and Euro 0–1 diesel vehicles. From 1 December 2026 an extension is announced for Euro 1 petrol vehicles registered before 1997 and Euro 2 diesels registered before 2001, subject to the city’s exceptions and conditions. For an older car, check its emissions class and any exemption before travelling. City of Florence — ZTL and Scudo Verde . Tolls: many motorways use toll booths, but barrier-free sections also exist. Unpaid journeys on Pedemontana Lombarda must be paid within the following 15 calendar days. Operator’s payment rules .
